t:
That section 5(a) of the Employment Act of 1946 (15 U.S.C. 1024(a)) is amended to read as follows:


“(a) 
There is established a Joint Economic Committee, to be composed of ten Members of the Senate, to be appointed by the President of the Senate, and ten Members of the House of Representatives, to be appointed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives. In each case, the majority party shall be represented by six Members and the minority party shall be represented by four Members.”

fable.w: The tempting reading is that establishing a "Committee" with appointed members is an advisory body and therefore participation. That fails because the Joint Economic Committee is composed entirely of Senators and Representatives, who are inside the federal government. No state, expert, company, or member of the public is brought into any federal decision, and the section provides for no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: There is established a Joint Economic Committee, to be composed of ten Members of the Senate, to be appointed by the President of the Senate, and ten Members of the House of Representatives

qwen_block.w: The section establishes a committee composed entirely of Members of Congress (Senate and House of Representatives). According to the definition, Congress and its members are inside the federal government. Therefore, a committee consisting solely of federal legislators does not involve participation by people outside the government.
qwen_block.s: There is established a Joint Economic Committee, to be composed of ten Members of the Senate, to be appointed by the President of the Senate, and ten Members of the House of Representatives, to be appointed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives.

opus.w: The committee is made up only of Members of the Senate and House, who are all inside the federal government. The section sets up how the committee is formed and who sits on it. It involves no states, experts, the public or other outside parties in any federal decision. The word 'Committee' might look like an advisory panel, but there are no non-federal members, so this is not participation.
opus.s: There is established a Joint Economic Committee, to be composed of ten Members of the Senate, to be appointed by the President of the Senate, and ten Members of the House of Representatives, to be appointed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives.
opus.b: This is **No**. The section creates a "Joint Economic Committee", which can look like an advisory body with outside members. But every member is a Senator or Representative, and Members of Congress are inside the federal government. No outside party is consulted or brought into a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section establishes a committee composed entirely of Members of Congress (Senators and Representatives). According to the definition, Congress and its members are inside the federal government. There is no requirement or recommendation for consultation or coordination with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or experts).
qwen_chat.s: There is established a Joint Economic Committee, to be composed of ten Members of the Senate, to be appointed by the President of the Senate, and ten Members of the House of Representatives, to be appointed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives.
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the committee includes Members of Congress, and Congress is part of the federal government, this is just internal government structure. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress is INSIDE the federal government. The key question is whether *outside* parties are involved. Here, the committee is composed entirely of Senators and Representatives. There is no mention of public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states/tribes/public. Therefore, it is internal.

Wait, let me re-read the definition carefully.
"Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government... Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government."
"Answer 'No' for these common traps: reports to, or notifications of, Congress... Congress is inside the federal government"

The section establishes a Joint Economic Committee composed of Senators and Representatives. These are federal officials. There is no interaction with outsiders described in this specific text snippet. It is purely an internal legislative body creation.

Therefore, the label is No.
